newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Argentina's Kiguel on bond issue-RFTV.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Argentina's Kiguel on bond issue-RFTV.

text.p: After increasing a global bond issue to $1.0 billion on Wednesday, Argentina needed $2.0 billion to meet its 1996 financing needs, and expected to tap the yen and lira markets for its remaining external borrowings, an Argentince finance official said Tuesday.

Manuel Kiguel, Argentine undersecretary of finance, told Reuters Financial Television that the country would look to raise about half its remaining 1996 debt on local markets and the rest internationally.
"One of our objectives is to tap the yen market by the end of the year,' Kiguel said. "We might tap the Lira market. Most likely we will not go back to the Yankee market this year.'
Kiguel said the ministry decided to raise the issue sizew to $1.0 billion from $750 million after investors oversubscribed to the issue by three times.
"The terms of the deal were very good for the republic so we decided to increase the deal to $1.0 billion in order to satisfy demand,' Kiguel said.
With the warm reception to the bond, Argentina may turn to the U.S. markets more frequently in the future, Kiguel said.
"In 1996 most of our financing was in the German mark market, but we think that's going to change,' he said.
He said that the govenrment expected the deal would price at the lower end of price talk, which pegged the deal at 445-450 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries.

Given the investor interest, the global bands should trade higher when they reach the seconodary market, he said, adding that the country was sensitive to concerns that previous Argentine bonds have weakened after pricing.
"We'll continue to look for the best deal (for Argentina), but we will also try to satisfy investors so that they feel happy with Argentina bonds and buy them again," he said.
"We had demand from hedge funds and traders, but most of the demand fortunately for us came from very stable buy-and- hold clients -- insurance companies, pension funds," he said.
